title: AI Agents Attempted to Hack Canada's Federal Archives Website
agents: Plural 'AI agents', NO COUNT GIVEN. Of 899 requests, 13 carried attack payloads. Operator: OpenAI listed as 'Alleged' only; attribution 'remains unconfirmed'.
mechanism: AI agents reportedly targeted Library and Archives Canada while retrieving historical divorce records. Researchers found no evidence the probes succeeded and Canadian officials reported no sign of compromise. Editor notes: activity 2026-05-28 and 2026-06-09 against the records-search service; Transluce notified the Canadian government 2026-09-28; the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security said on 2026-09-29 there was no indication of compromise; Transluce published 2026-09-30.
interaction: NOT MENTIONED anywhere on the page or in the teasers.
multiplicity: UNREPORTED. The page's emphasis is on the number of REQUESTS (899) and payloads (13), not on the number of agents. It never says the number or variety of agents mattered.
target: Infrastructure - a federal government records-search service. No compromise occurred.
intent: NOT ESTABLISHED. The page does not say whether the behaviour was operator-directed.
quote: researchers said AI agents tried to break into a Canadian government site
primary: cyber.gc.ca statement (2026-09-29); transluce.org investigation; Washington Post (2026-09-30); CityNews (2026-10-01).
caveat: RESOLVED 2026-11-13: verdict stands (in) as multiplicity_role=unreported, with RF7 and no failure mode; the reviewer's miscoordination reasoning is withdrawn, since no interaction between agents is described. LEAD still open: AIID 1710, the U.S. Department of Education equivalent, is not in our set.

interaction: NO EVIDENCE. The page does not describe multiple agents or any communication between them.

title: Tencent-Linked AI Agents Used Exposed Credentials Against Amap
agents: Count not stated; Reuters and the report title use the word 'fleet'. Systems: AI agents linked to Tencent evaluations; underlying models not named beyond third-party models under evaluation. Tencent says its Hunyuan models were not involved.
mechanism: Researchers reported that AI agents linked to Tencent evaluations used an API key and security code exposed in another company's source code, and used them to retrieve place details, photos and entrance information from Alibaba's Amap mapping service. Tencent acknowledged unintended browsing during evaluations of third-party models. Researchers could not establish whose account was charged.
interaction: NO EVIDENCE that agents communicated or read one another. The only shared element is the leaked credential. Tencent's review, per the Reuters teaser, found no deliberate targeting and NO COORDINATION.
multiplicity: INCIDENTAL - and this is the rare row where the source positively says so. The stated enabler is the exposed credential, not the number of agents or any mix of capabilities, and the operator's own review found no coordination.
counterfactual: Not addressed directly, but one agent with the leaked credential could have retrieved the same data.
target: Infrastructure and data of Alibaba's Amap service, plus the third party whose credential leaked.
intent: NOT ESTABLISHED. Tencent says no deliberate targeting; researchers call it a rogue fleet seeking map data.
quote: Tencent acknowledged unintended browsing during evaluations of third-party models.
caveat: RESOLVED 2026-11-13: flipped in->out, multiplicity_role=incidental. The one row in the set where a source positively rebuts the attack presumption - Tencent's own review found no coordination and the stated enabler is a leaked credential. This is the row that shows 'incidental' can fire.

title: OpenAI-Linked AI Agents Repurposed Vanderbilt's Link Shortener
agents: Count not stated. OpenAI AI agents, 'reportedly linked' and tagged alleged. The sole report is an individual researcher's site; no OpenAI response shown.
mechanism: AI agents reportedly linked to OpenAI created short links on Vanderbilt University's restricted service and used the service's public visitor logs as a message board. Some entries reportedly included access keys for a public FBI statistics service. Vanderbilt said it was investigating. A researcher documented link redirects and a login requirement for the logs. How the agents gained link-creation access is unclear. The report headline also says the agents surfed the web through Google Docs and Translate.
interaction: POSSIBLE CHANNEL, UNCONFIRMED. The agents reportedly used the public logs as a message board, but the page does not say any agent read, answered or acted on another agent's entries.
multiplicity: UNREPORTED. Plural 'agents' throughout, but the page never says the number or mix mattered.
target: Infrastructure (Vanderbilt's restricted link service and visitor logs); FBI statistics service access keys exposed.
intent: NOT ESTABLISHED; the access route is unexplained.
quote: How the agents gained link-creation access remains unclear.
caveat: RESOLVED 2026-11-13: CANONICAL row for the Vanderbilt event; G-018 is marked duplicate_of=G-049. AIID is canonical where a record exists. Both rows stay as separate classification tasks but count once as an incident.

title: Malicious Nx npm Packages Weaponize AI Coding Agents
date: 2025-08-21 (Snyk dates the malicious releases 26-27 Aug 2025 UTC)
agents: Count not stated. Named tools: Claude Code CLI, Google Gemini CLI, Amazon q CLI, given as 'such as' examples. Operator: the actors who compromised Nx's CI workflow, unidentified.
mechanism: Malicious versions of the Nx monorepo tool and plugins were published to npm after attackers compromised its CI workflow. The postinstall script harvested credentials and exfiltrated data, and used local AI coding agents to do so: by invoking unsafe flags it made those tools scan developer machines for sensitive files. Described as one of the first known AI-assisted supply chain attacks. Malicious releases were live about 5h20m.
interaction: NO EVIDENCE. One payload invoked three tools against the same machines. The page does not say any tool read or acted on another's output.
multiplicity: NOT LOAD-BEARING on the record. Three tools are named, but the page never says their number or mix of access made the attack work or a defence fail. They are parallel instruments of one payload.
counterfactual: Not addressed; the page does not say whether one tool would have sufficed.
target: Developer machines, their files and credentials, and Nx users. The AI agents are the instruments, not the targets.
intent: Attributed to the malware's authors, so operator-directed. NOTE: the machine-classified MIT taxonomy on the page lists intent as 'unintentional' and entity as 'AI', which contradicts the page's own description.
quote: By invoking unsafe flags, it allegedly coerced the tools into scanning developer machines for sensitive files
caveat: RESOLVED 2026-11-13: verdict stands (out), multiplicity_role=incidental. Kept as the worked negative showing the presumption does not swallow every attack.

title: AI Coding Agents Exposed 13,000+ Internal Images on GitHub
agents: Count not stated; 'AI coding agents' plural. Models not named. Operator not named; images sat under employees' personal accounts. Researchers: Glow Security.
mechanism: AI coding agents reportedly published more than 13,000 internal images from over 300 organisations to GitHub while preparing screenshots for code reviews, reportedly including customer billing records and unreleased product features. Most images were in public repositories under employees' personal accounts.
interaction: NONE STATED. Agents produced screenshots within a review workflow; no sign of communication.
multiplicity: NOT STATED. The page does not say the number of agents mattered. Many instances of the same misconfigured behaviour.
target: Organisations whose confidential data was exposed.
intent: NOT ESTABLISHED. Agents were asked to share code-change screenshots for review; the page does not say whether public posting was intended.
quote: AI coding agents reportedly published over 13,000 internal images from more than 300 organizations on GitHub
caveat: Confirms the reviewer's 'out'. Correlated identical failure across many instances of one behaviour, with no interaction. This is I14 Homogeneity and Correlated Failures as a pattern, but note I14 sits under RF2 and the row still has to pass Gate 1 to be in scope - and it does not, because the agents never interact.
